justifications.functional_suitability: Consultation Service (signaling, Media Relay Proxy), Prescription & Interoperability Service, AI Symptom Orchestrator and Consent Controller cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: the symptom checker is modeled as an external system, and the clinician-patient scheduling and pharmacy-country routing logic is not explicit.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Memorystore Ephemeral Session Cache, SFU Media Relay Proxy, pgBouncer, asynchronous Audit Logger event publishing and the GraphQL Complexity Analyzer help. Gaps: no autoscaling, no explicit capacity or latency targets, and the synchronous consent check sits on the AI request path.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR Adapter Component (HAPI FHIR) covers the US, and EU E-Prescription Gateway Component (Apache Camel) covers national standards, both over mTLS. Circuit Breaker / Resilience Interceptor isolates pharmacy failures. Gap: no per-country EU adapters are shown.
justifications.usability: Patient Web App, Patient Mobile App and Clinician Portal serve both user groups. The Local State Manager gives offline-first support and WebRTC Media Engine handles low-bandwidth video. Gaps: no consent-management UI, no accessibility or localization, and no pharmacist interface.
justifications.reliability: Degraded Mode Fallback Controller in Media Relay Proxy addresses R-06, and the Circuit Breaker, DLQs in Pub/Sub, the audit WAL buffer and the Local State Manager add resilience. Gaps: no multi-zone or failover/DR design, no backups, no RTO/RPO, and the fail-closed consent path hurts availability.
justifications.security: Strong mechanisms: Istio mTLS with SPIFFE, IAP, OAuth2/OIDC Auth & Scope Middleware, Consent Token Issuer, OPA Compliance Enforcement Engine, regional CMEK in GCP KMS, WORM Medical Document Store, INSERT-only audit logging, and KMS-signed AI logs with model version pinning.
justifications.maintainability: Clear service decomposition with separate responsibilities (Consent & Audit Service, AI Symptom Orchestrator, Prescription adapters). Interfaces are gRPC with GitOps via ArgoCD, and adapters are replaceable. Gaps: the shared Data & Cache Stores container couples services, the component models are inconsistent, and a polyglot stack adds overhead.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes, Istio, ArgoCD, OPA and External Secrets Operator are portable and per-region ArgoCD planes are provided. However, the design is strongly tied to GCP services (Cloud SQL, Memorystore, KMS, IAP, GCS, Pub/Sub) with no abstraction layer, and no IaC or multi-cloud strategy is shown.

tradeoffs: SFU scalability vs media encryption and recording overhead
PERF-01.justification: SFU relay, Redis session state and Istio exist, but no autoscaling, capacity sizing or regional deployment of media nodes is described. The 5,000 concurrent sessions and 10 s join time are plausible but unaddressed.

elements: Audit & Traceability Logger Component with KMS Signing Interceptor
sensitivity_points: Synchronous consent check on every request
tradeoffs: Fail-closed consent and signed audit vs latency
PERF-02.justification: The synchronous consent call, KMS signing and an external engine sit in the request path. The audit is asynchronous with a WAL, but there is no caching, autoscaling or capacity design for about 14 requests/s, and no latency budget is given.

sensitivity_points: Sync of offline notes after reconnect
tradeoffs: Offline caching vs device data security
AVAIL-01.justification: A Degraded Mode Fallback Controller and an encrypted offline-first local store address the need. But no adaptive bitrate, audio-only fallback, reconnect or note-sync mechanism is specified, so no-loss of notes is unproven.

AVAIL-02.justification: Regional isolation preserves residency, but no multi-zone or standby US design, backup/restore or DR runbook is described. The brief gives only one region per jurisdiction, so recovery within 1 hour is unsupported; ArgoCD redeploy is the only path.

sensitivity_points: Single EU gateway for all countries
Domain model common to all standards
tradeoffs: Adapter isolation vs duplicated per-country mapping logic
MOD-01.justification: Standards are isolated in adapter components behind the domain controller and resilience interceptor. A new country means a new adapter, though the EU gateway is one component and may need an internal split.

elements: Audit & Traceability Logger Component with KMS Signing Interceptor
sensitivity_points: Model version recorded per log entry
MOD-02.justification: Immutable version pinning, signed logs with inputs and WORM storage support traceability. Rollback and runtime version switching are not explicitly described, but pinning makes them feasible.

sensitivity_points: Cross-region call path to the US data
Consent token validation at every service
tradeoffs: Strict regional isolation vs clinician cross-border workflows
SEC-01.justification: A compliance engine with OPA, consent tokens, scope middleware, regional routing and Gatekeeper residency checks deny access without consent, and an append-only audit exists. The cross-region request flow is not fully explicit.

tradeoffs: Short-lived tokens vs token issuance load
SEC-02.justification: Short-lived consent tokens and per-purpose consent management naturally limit sharing, and audit supports verification. But no explicit revocation propagation, research-data sharing flow or downstream cutoff is shown.
